# CHTC Campus Computing Documentation

> Guides for using the Center for High Throughput Computing's UW-Madison campus computing services: the High Throughput Computing (HTC) system and the High Performance Computing (HPC) cluster.

Full text of every guide: https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/llms-full.txt

## HTC guides

- [System Overview](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/htc-overview/): The CHTC high-throughput computing (HTC) cluster provides support a variety of computational research tasks. The HTC system offers CPUs/GPUs, high-memory nodes, and other specialized hardware.…
- [Roadmap to getting started](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/htc-roadmap/): This roadmap shows the main steps for getting started on CHTC's HTC system. Use this page as a starting point, review key concepts, and find links to more detailed guides.
- [Log in to CHTC](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/connecting/): This guide outlines login information for CHTC services, including how to log in to CHTC servers after your account has been created, access point information, and how to re-use ssh connections to…

- [Submitting Multiple Jobs Using HTCondor](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/multiple-jobs/): This guide shows you how to write a submit file to submit multiple jobs. This option is great for submitting high throughput workloads, such as iterating over multiple datasets or parameters.

- [Use Software Available in Modules](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/htc-modules/): This guide describes when and how to use software, using MPI as an example, that is available as pre-installed modules on the HTC system.
- [Checkpointing Jobs](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/checkpointing/): Some jobs may take many hours or even days to finish. If one of these jobs is interrupted or reaches a runtime limit, it could lose all of its progress and need to start over.

- [Intermediate DAGMan: Uses and Features](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/htc/tutorial-dagman-intermediate/): This tutorial helps you explore HTCondor's DAGMan and its many features. Download the tutorial files from Github.

- [Interactive GPU Jobs](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/htc-interactive-gpu-jobs/): This guide shows you how to run interactive GPU jobs on CHTC's High Throughput Computing (HTC) system.
- [Scale Beyond Local HTC Capacity](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/scaling-htc/): This guide provides an introduction to running jobs outside of CHTC: why using these resources is beneficial, what resources are available, and how to use them.
- [Submit High Memory Jobs](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/high-memory-jobs/): The examples and information in the below guide areuseful ONLY if: - you already have an account on a CHTC-administered submit server - your jobs will use more than ~120 GB of memory

- [Known Issues on the HTC](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/htc-known-issues/): This page documents some common and known issues encountered on the HTC system. While this page can be beneficial in troubleshooting, it does not contain a comprehensive list of errors.
- [Request variable memory](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/variable-memory/): This page outlines strategies for requesting variable amounts of memory in jobs. This guide is for users whose memory usage for a list of jobs may spike unexpectedly or vary depending on inputs or…

- [Get Help](https://chtc.cs.wisc.edu/uw-research-computing/get-help/): We provide general support via email. You can typically expect a first response within 1-2 business days.
